Paddy Pimblett vs Benoit St-Denis is a high-variance, fan-friendly lightweight matchup, and I’d give the edge to Paddy Pimblett by late submission or decision, with the most likely finish being a submission in rounds 3-4.

Official pick: Paddy Pimblett
Method/time: Submission, Round 4, around 2:30
Confidence: 6.5/10

Why: Paddy’s recent form has aged well. He just went 5 hard rounds with Justin Gaethje, then before that showed real finishing progression with a third-round TKO of Michael Chandler and a quick technical submission of King Green. That tells you two things: his cardio is good enough to keep a dangerous pace, and his opportunistic grappling is still a major weapon when opponents overextend. Against BSD, that matters because St-Denis is aggressive, explosive, and very dangerous early, but he can also be drawn into scrambles and over-commit to pressure.

Style matchup: BSD is the stronger “must-fight-now” athlete here, with the nastier early finishing profile and a clear ability to hurt people fast. His run through Hooker, Dariush, Ruffy, and Prepolec shows he’s become much more than just a pressure grappler. But Paddy’s combination of composure, craft, and submission threat is the cleaner long-game answer. If he survives the first big storm, he should be able to make BSD work in longer exchanges, where Paddy’s pace management and opportunistic clinch/grappling transitions become more valuable.

Finish profile: BSD’s best window is rounds 1-2, especially if he can force chaos and make Paddy reset often. Paddy’s best window is rounds 2-4, when BSD’s pressure can become a little more open and Paddy can capitalize on scrambles, front headlock threats, and back takes.

Key uncertainty: BSD’s explosiveness is a real problem, and if he lands clean early he can absolutely flip the fight. The main swing factor is whether Paddy can stay disciplined through the first round without giving BSD the kind of layered grappling chaos that leads to top control or damage. If he does, I favor Paddy’s durability and submission game to take over late.

St-Denis is the more violent finisher on paper and has been hot with wins over Hooker, Dariush, and Ruffy, but he’s also been in more chaotic fights and has shown he can be cracked when the pace and exchanges get messy.

Style-wise, this is a classic pressure vs scrambling matchup. BSD is dangerous if he can force front-half grappling and turn it into clinch damage or a quick submission chain, but Pimblett’s submission game is underrated and his conditioning/pace over three rounds makes him more live to bank the second and third if he survives the early storm. In a 3-rounder, I lean Paddy’s ability to absorb the first wave, get the fight into layered grappling, and win minutes.

Finish profile: Pimblett by late sub is still live, but the reduced distance makes decision the cleaner call.
Key uncertainty: early BSD violence. If St-Denis lands hard early or gets top position fast, the whole read can flip quickly.
